utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next witness is a witness with no protective measures. It's Witness T-6, Mr. Vlajko Bozic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the blind is still down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please see to it that the blind is drawn up.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, the blind needs to remain down until the transcript pages scroll through because there remains private information on the transcript which is viewable from the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We have been put in our place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you please tell the Judges your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: My name is Vlajko Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have already warned you, even before you entered the courtroom, not to answer a single question even if it's a question of just a few words until the text on the monitor stops. You were born on the 30th of October, 1958; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were born in Sokolac in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You attended elementary school and high school for catering in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You served your military term of duty in the JNA in 1985, and you had the rank of a lieutenant in reserve?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When the conflict broke out, you were a representative of the Prosvjeta publishing house from Belgrade in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you lived in your family house in the settlement of Jagomir, the municipality of Centar, in Sarajevo, just below Grdonj hill?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to put a question to you right at the beginning. You were a member of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, as fighter of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, or perhaps you had some sort of a command duty, throughout the war you were in Jagomir below Grdonj, close to the so-called Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But at the beginning I still need to ask you a few things or put questions to you that have to do with your joining the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and for that reason I would like to ask you to explain to the Court first what happened in Sarajevo in late 1991 and early 1992.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In late 1991 or in early 1992, the situation in Sarajevo was very tense in terms of interethnic relations, and all of this resulted in a war and the break-up of the former Yugoslavia. The war began in Slovenia, Croatia. Everybody was expecting for something to happen in Bosnia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please go more slowly? Otherwise, most of what you say will not be transcribed.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I personally didn't think that the conflict in Bosnia would be of a large scale, because all sensible people, having seen what happened in Slovenia and Croatia, would not allow this to happen in Bosnia and Herzegovina as well. Unfortunately, what happened, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened? How long did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I went to work until the 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened on the 6th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, 1992, I received telephone information from the Territorial Defence city headquarters of the municipality of Centar to report to the post office because I did have a war assignment as a commander of the military police, and the place where we were supposed to assemble was called Velesici. I got to the building of the TO, and that's where I saw some members of the Green Berets with weapons who were securing the building, which wasn't making sense to me, because I knew that the Green Berets were formed by the Party for Democratic Action to protect themselves, and in exactly what way became obvious later during the war. When I entered the building, I was supposed to report to a room on the second floor. In front of the door I saw some 10 people whom I recognised who were waiting to report just like I did, and I saw some active officers on the -- in the corridor, active-duty officers, and I recognised that by their uniform. And I recognised someone who at the time was -- had the rank of a captain or something, Hajnandzic [phoen]. And it wasn't logical to me that there would be so many active-duty officers in the Territorial Defence headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a captain or Major Hajnandzic. Later on during the war, was he promoted to a high office in the military during the war later on?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he got the rank of general during the war or after the war. I don't know. But I know that on the 31st of July, 1992, he signed the decision or the order to launch an attack in Gromila and Poljine and Bitanja [phoen] area which was the Defence area manned by the battalion where I was. And that's when we actually captured those documents. I don't know where those documents are now, but perhaps measures could be taken to find those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what was he at the end the war in the 1st Corps of the BH army? What post did he hold?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I'm not sure. I can't tell you exactly what post he had there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could speed things up relating to those general matters? What happened later when you arrived there? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I just turned around and went back home, because I saw that the situation was not as it should have been. On that day in the afternoon, the Green Berets carried out an attack from the Grdonj area to the village of Nikolici, and the first casualty fell on that day Nedeljko Dragas, he was the father of my sister-in-law, my brother's wife. So this is when the war started for us who lived there in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, what did you do, and what did the other people from this area do? How did you get weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning we had whatever weapons people owned. Some pistols, some hunting rifles. There were some people who bought weapons. There was a lively trade in -- a lively smuggling trade in weapons. And we got some weapons when the people, the villagers -- it was not an organised action of any sort. When we went into the depots, military depots in the Faletici barracks and got some of the weapons from there. I think it was sometime in late April, but I'm not quite sure. I can't really tell you when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It was just the people from this area where you lived or was there somebody else too?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, Muslims took some of those weapons. I can't really tell you how much went to each party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened at that time in the police force?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, a conflict broke out or, rather, the police got divided into the Muslim or Bosniak and Serbian police, so that we got some of the weapons from the reserve force of the police of Serb ethnic background who were members or who -- rather, who were in service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when did the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps or the Republika Srpska army became -- become operational? When did you join this corps?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Republika Srpska army started functioning in May or, rather, in June 1992. As for the exact date for the inception of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, I cannot really tell you that. And as for my unit, the unit where I was, at first it was an independent detachment. In other words, we did not rely on anyone for support. We relied only on ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say that you relied only on yourselves, what are you trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to tell you that we did not have any active-duty officers from the Yugoslav People's Army in our ranks. There were several of us who were reserve officers. And we didn't have anything to do with the army at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just tell us very briefly what brigade you belonged to or whether you held any posts. If you can, just very briefly, so that the Chamber is able to tell what unit you were in in Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I was in the Kosevo Brigade of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. After I was wounded in 1992, that was on the 8th of June, I spent 45 days in the hospital. And when I left hospital as one of the two reserve officers, I was appointed the commander of the 2nd Battalion in the Kosevo Brigade. And I held that post until April 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And thereafter?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This was when reorganisation took place, and three brigades, Kosevo, Vogosca, and Rajlovac were reorganised to establish a single brigade, the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, and my battalion thus became the 1st Battalion of the Sarajevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do in that battalion? What duty did you perform there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, I was one of the assistants to the Chief of Staff of Operations -- for operations and training, but I spent most of my time in the field. And since I was from the Kosevo Brigade, I had come from the Kosevo Brigade, I mostly covered that area up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you say training, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: When you say training, it means some of the training. It covers some of the training of the fighters that we carried out during the cease-fire periods or at those times when there weren't so many engagements, combat engagements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And as for this training, what kind of military tasks did it encompass?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, once the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade was set up training started, and we worked with squads and platoons. We did training for defence activities for squads and platoons, and also we did training for the removal of heavy weapons to the area 20 kilometres away from the city as we obliged to according to the agreement. So we only did tactical defence activities. That's what we focused on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did you ever have any training for sniping activities?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you a document, and I will then complete my examination about this topic. That would be Prosecution Exhibit P683. Could you please look at this document, and could you focus on who issued this document and item 1, what this order is all about.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It was issued by the command of the SRK on the 19th of January, 1995. It's an order. Under item 1: "On the 23rd of January, 1995, transfer by 1000 hours the sniper instructors to the sector of the Jahorina barracks as follows."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to read all this. It's been before this Chamber several times. Under item 3, could you please see what does it say?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: "I appoint Captain Zoran Terzic and Lieutenant Vlajko Bozic to carry out the instruction and Major Stevan Veljovic to organise and oversee the completion of the course."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Judges, in light of this date, 19th of January, 1995, what was going on at the separation lines at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time from the 1st of January, 1995, the cease-fire was signed. I know that in this month a cease-fire was complied with because it was in winter and there was a lot of snow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Having told us this, that there was a lot of snow at that time, it says here that you were appointed to carry out the sniper instruction. Did you at all leave your post in light of what you told us and in light of where Jahorina is in relation to the position where you were?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: First of all, this is the first time that I see this order. And secondly, Mount Jahorina is a mountain, and in January and all the way up until March you can have up to two metres of snow. So I think that it is impossible to carry out any training of this kind in those conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the last item here, 4. Could you please read it, and then that would be it with this document.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: "The sniper instructors shall take with them their personal weapons, semi-automatic sniper rifles M-76, PASP, probably Rules of Service manual, equipment one b/k combat set of ammunition and sleeping bags. Adapt equipment to winter conditions on the mountain."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a sniper rifle at all?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you need any sniper rifles on those positions there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't need any sniper rifles on our positions, and we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what are sniper rifles used for in any military?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, sniper rifles in wartime in a military should be used to destroy military targets that are of great importance, major targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever get any oral or written order to target civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question to the witness. Mr. Witness, you are telling us that you have never seen this order. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only see the text in part. Are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the positions where you were, and now we will deal with that in more detail to explain to the Judges what I believe we need to explain, what weapons were available at the positions where you were to your unit?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Other than the infantry weapons, my unit didn't have any other weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what infantry weapons are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The automatic rifles, as well as, mortars of 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when you're talking about the weapons, you're talking about your Sarajevo-Romanjia Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you about the positions around Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd just like to get a clarification. Is the witness talking about his unit, in other words, his battalion, or the brigade, in other words, the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, because the initial question was with respect to his unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what are you talking about, Witness? Witness. Witness, what are you talking about? Is it your unit or your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We're going to go back to that. I would like to move directly to the problem. First let me ask you, which lines were you positioned at most frequently?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I most often was at Mrkovici, Grdonj, the Jagomir neighbourhood, and Poljine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were the separations like at Grdonj, Jagomir, and Mrkovic?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In order to -- for us to understand each other and for the Judges to understand, I would like to show you, and I think it would be easier and more useful for the Trial Chamber, I would like to show you a map -- or, rather, a photograph, 65 ter 03426, and then we can deal with these matters in the most direct way. Do you see the photograph?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, can you please tell me where this neighbourhood was where you lived, where you had your family house? You mentioned Jagomir.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Is there a marker or something? This part is called Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, take a slowly, because I didn't ask you that.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: My house is behind the hill some 800 metres or a thousand metres behind the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you please wait for the question. Can you please mark approximately where in relation to this circle that you marked would be your house.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw an arrow indicating where your house would be. And does that mean that your house was at the end of this arrow?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you circle that place, please and mark it with the letter "K".

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this circle that you've drawn, you said that was Grdonj. And can you please place the letter "G" in the middle of the circle.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the conflict, what was your route that you took to go to work, to go to town? Can you please mark this route that you would usually take?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The route actually -- or the road led from my house, but you cannot see it because it's behind this hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is there another route, another road that you could use to go to town and to work? Do you see it here?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it. It's right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Everything that you point to, can you also please mark. Mark it with the letter "P", please.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When the conflict broke out, when you took up weapons, were you able to use that road at all?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When the conflict began, did you manage to make some sort of communication with those areas that you had some connection with?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: When the conflicts began, we had a sort of mountain path. In order to have a real road, we made this road that you can see on the photograph here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you draw it in the other direction, please.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the entire length of the road, if it's possible to see it on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's possible. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us this arrow, where does that point to?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: To Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So can you mark that with the letter "V". At the other end, where did the road lead to?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that with the letter "P", please.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now, was there a line of separation there in military -- in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate the line of separation on this map dividing you? Actually, if you could be -- could you please use a different colour to mark this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be given a different coloured marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: First, I would like you to mark the lines where the positions of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark those positions all along this photograph.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that with the letter "L".

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, where were the positions of your unit -- or, rather, the units that belonged to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me, this second middle line in relation to the ridge of this hill, below this line where were the positions?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Are you thinking of this ridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark it.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: If you're talking about this ridge --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you do that first.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: They were about 50 to 70 metres behind the ridge. At least 50 metres behind this ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark this second red line with the letter "S".

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now can you please tell us Grdonj that we see here, it doesn't have a single tree on it. During the conflict, what was it like? What was on the hill? Did it look like this?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No. A part of the hill, perhaps a half of it, was wooded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate that section with a circle and place the letter "P" in that circle.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me which units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were located there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In this area along the lines of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina there were two brigades that were active. I'm not sure if it was the 105th or the 109th, but I know that this area was covered by two brigades. And the objective was to fire constantly and put pressure along our lines of defence with the objective of cutting this road and capturing this area and to put pressure on Vogosca and to capture the Pretis factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell the Judges what the conflicts or the clashes were like when they occurred. And how often did they occur throughout that period, particularly in the period from August 1994, until the end the conflict.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The pressure on this sector of our unit's lines was constant, but the greatest intensity was during September and October 1994, in June and July 1995, in relation to some other actions that were being carried out in other parts of the theatre, but the pressure was constant. I cannot say that the fighting was conducted every day, but practically there was combat every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate which position in particular was exposed to this? Can you show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: What you can see here is a building or facility built by the Austro-Hungarian army, and we called that Mala Kula, Little Tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please point that out?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It was behind the ridge. And then in the forest there is another Austro-Hungarian building which was called Velika Kula, Large Tower. That's when the most pressure was felt. These were buildings specially built for the Austrian army, so it was not so easy to resist such pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the place where the conflicts most often were located, and if we take into account the distances that you mentioned earlier, what was the dominant position in this whole area that is shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This part of the area shown on this photograph, the highest peak is this one here. This is elevation 906, and it overlooks this side from here. It overlooks the ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Finish the arrow and mark what you have just drawn with the letter "G".

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when you mentioned the elevation for this feature marked by a circle, can you please write in on the left side of the circle the elevation and its height. You said --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: 906, that's what we called it. It's a feature with an altitude of 906 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please write that down.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me which weapons you had when you were at these positions. First of all, can you tell me what the positions consisted of when you were there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Here at elevation 906 was the position of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Distance from this elevation to the Mala Kula where we were is 120 metres. I know that for a fact. Our positions were 50 metres behind the ridge. The ridge is about 60-odd metres high, and you can see that it slopes down gradually, and it is 200 metres in length. The top is about 20 metres broad, and then the slopes begin below that. So our positions were behind the ridge some 50 metres back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic. Mr. Tapuskovic, for the purpose of using this photo, I think it would be good if we could make better markings. I notice that both Grdonj and Spicasta Stijena are marked with a "G", which is confusing. And that neither Velika Kula nor Mala Kula have got any letters, and you may confuse which is which. So can I suggest that you, for instance, mark Spicasta Stijena with a "G1", or put another letter to it, I don't care, and then you could mark Velika Kula with a "V", and Mala Kula with an "M", or something of that sort, in order to be able to interpret the markings at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Harhoff, I will do that, but the witness marked it with letter "G" to indicate the ridge. It's Greban in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please mark -- use letter "O" here at the ridge.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Here at the ridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that here that is marked with letter "G" could you just make a circle that it becomes letter "O". And it seems here --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you see the little tower or not?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about the large tower?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can't see it because of the wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark this location where Mala Kula, Little Tower, is located.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You've marked this red line that's marked with little "L" as the positions of the BH army. What -- what's that? What was there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This line that I drew in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Listen to me. This thing that you marked with letter "L" down there, what is this? What was there? I don't want to lead you on this, but what were the BH army positions like?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's where the trenches were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: They're trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But who held the trenches on the other side?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, this line here marks the positions held by my unit, the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the other side --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and counsel please be asked to make pauses between question and answer for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. I'm not sure whether you heard the interpreter. She's asking that the witness and counsel observe pauses between question and answer, otherwise it's very difficult for the interpreter. Don't overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We really have to take that into account. I myself started going a bit faster. You told us that the intention on most cases -- in most cases had been to cut this communication. My first question to you is, what weapons did you have in the trenches that you held?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, apart from the semi-automatic and automatic rifles we didn't have anything else. We had our personal weapons and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And did you have any heavy weapons with you in the trenches?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And did the BH army have any major weapons at the 906 elevation?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, they had an anti-aircraft cannon that was used by them to target this communication line. I don't know whether they had anything else, but I'm sure about this anti-aircraft cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And if we look at the right-hand side positions held by the BH army that you drew in, what is the configuration of the terrain there in relation to the red line that you marked all the way to the edge when you spoke about the lines held by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, this picture does not really correspond to the actual situation. This part here is -- it's a hill. It's green here, but it's not a wooded area, and I marked this with a -- a line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please stop. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so that the Court is able to be precise as to what the witness is saying, when the witness says this mark here, this part over there, and I can't see where the witness is pointing to, and I submit that this is actually quite important to know what the witness is saying. So perhaps he could have a pointer and we could see on the screen which part he refers to when he says this part here and this part there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Witness, in your answer said, "This part here, it's a hill." Can you show us with the pointer where that is? We see --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please circle it.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark this with the letter "V", this part that you circled just now. We already have a "V" for Vogosca. Could you please then mark it with a "W"?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please draw another line here. Is there anything between this feature 906 that you marked and this ridge? Is there anything in between that you could describe and if there is could you please draw a line.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, between 906 feature and this ridge there's nothing. There is line of sight between the two. You can see from one to the other, no obstacles there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened -- what happened with the vehicles that were driving along this road going to Pale in one direction and to Vogosca in the other? What happened to those cars when they would pass by this area?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Whenever any movement of vehicles would be observed on this road, fire was opened and both the vehicles and the people inside were in danger, and quite often it would happen. And people would get shot in those vehicles. People would get killed. So this road could be used only at night, at dusk, or at dawn in the early morning hours. And people did all they could to avoid driving along it by day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just mark one more thing. What were the positions from which this road was targeted, and could you just draw some arrows indicating that towards the road.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The most effective targeting of this road was carried out from the summit of this hill marked as 906, because it was the dominant height. It dominated this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with the letter "Sh". And what other direction was also a possibility to target this road?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, from this hill here. From this hill here that's marked with "W".

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And could you just tell me one more thing. At the front lines during the conflict and while you lived there, did you suffer any casualties?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Let me just tell you one thing. During the war from 1992 until the end of 1995, while there was fighting our unit suffered casualties. About 550 of our fighters were killed and several hundred civilians were killed too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this map be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D318, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to see a photograph, and let us deal with it as briefly as possible. It's marked C19. Let us deal with it briefly, and I would like you to show us, to draw the separation lines indicating the positions where the BH army had its trenches and the positions where the Republika Srpska army had its trenches. Yes, this part. Page 13. This is what we see in front of us, page 13 of the court photographs C11. Could you please draw a line indicating the trenches of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the SRK trenches, where were they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now that you drew this, could you please tell us what was the distance since you said that this was behind the hill. What was the distance from the ridge?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It was about a hundred to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From the positions. You told us a little while ago something that was a bit different.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the Republika Srpska army trenches, the positions of the trenches of the SRK.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: From the separation line what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I asked you -- that's what you already told us. How far were the SRK trenches from the top of the ridge?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: At least 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Judges -- well, you said about 50 metres, and you said more at places but the only thing that got recorded was 50 metres. So what is the correct answer?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I said at least 50 metres, and in some areas even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. On this photograph you can see -- I can't really define it, but if you look at elevation 906 and then if you go to the right a little bit, what is it that you can see here? There is a thing that I wouldn't like to define it. I heard from some witnesses what it is, but is there an area that you could perhaps call by some name or whatever it is that you do things when you're dealing with natural phenomena.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to this position here, this part here? Could you please tell me what area are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to show you from here, but is there some kind of a wedge here?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, in this area, yeah, I'm sure there must be some wedges.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us? Could you please draw it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this gully here, the first one, what were the positions of the trenches? But let us first mark those lines. The first line, could you please mark it with letters "ABiH", and the other one there with "SRK". And I would like to ask you something that I really need to ask you and I don't want to dwell on this because you've already clarified. From elevation 906, what did this elevation dominate or control?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The elevation 906 controlled the whole area of Mrkovici, Jagomir, Radova, Pionirska Dolina, and Kromolj, those neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Sedrenik. Well, they could control Sedrenik. It was in the territory that the BH army held.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And just to deal with this photograph, to avoid any misunderstandings, could you please write the words "Iza Brda" behind the hill where you marked SRK.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to tender this photograph as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just like the witness -- well, I withdraw that. I'll do it in cross-examination. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D319, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a question for clarification purposes. Are we far from Grdonj hill? This elevation in relation to Grdonj hill, how far is it? Can we see Grdonj hill on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark Grdonj here. Could you mark it here with a circle.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The photograph just disappeared from my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does that mean that we have lost all the markings?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it doesn't. We save it and it will be just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now in light of the question that His Honour Judge Mindua asked, could you please circle Grdonj here.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please mark the elevation. How high is it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It's 906 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So from this position you can control all those areas that you indicated?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see from this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the heavy weapons that the BH army had was positioned in those areas?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to that elevation, all the elevations held by the army of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, that last question about the heavy weapons in my submission is leading and, in my recollection, mischaracterises the evidence. I understand that the witness spoke about an anti-aircraft weapon, and I don't know if he went into further details about other weapons. I may be mistaken, but that's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it was leading, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was convinced that I asked him about something he already said, but I can repeat my question. I asked what heavy weapons were at that location, and he can again say that. I was citing him, so maybe I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were the heavy weapons that were located at this 906 elevation of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Elevation 906 had an anti-aircraft gun. There was definitely one. Perhaps it was 20- or 30-millimetre calibre, and it was very effectively firing at the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to elevation 906, I need to ask you again. All the other positions occupied by your side, you, what position were they in?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see on the photograph that we were at a lower elevation in relation to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this photograph, can it please be saved and tendered as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Bozic, could you just clarify which road you refer to when you say that the anti-aircraft gun on top of Grdonj was controlling the road? Which road is that? Is that -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you cannot see the road on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That is exactly why I'm asking. So which road do you -- were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I explained that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Witness, let me be clear about it, because you can actually see some roads on the photo. So my question is, was the anti-aircraft gun on top of Grdonj placed in such a manner as to point away from what we can see in the picture, that is to say, in the other direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Harhoff, I need to put one more question, then, in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How many kilometres behind Grdonj was that road, your road that led to Pale and Vogosca? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The closest road from elevation 906, or the distance between elevation 906 and the road at some places was at least 200 to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please draw a line from one end to the other end of this road? Above the ridge, a little bit higher up. Some 3 to 4 centimetres higher.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You can do that. And then draw a long line, and in the other direction as well, please.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You can also please draw a line towards Grdonj from the road.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And next to that you can place the numbers 200 to 400.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And mark that line with the letter "T".

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the shorter line you can mark with the letter "O".

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of the line can you please draw in arrows, and you can put the letter "P" there, and on the other end you can place the letter "V" like you did before.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we please save this, and I would like to tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, I have one more question. I hope it's the last one, because I don't want to disrupt your examination-in-chief. Witness, please, you say that on Grdonj hill there was an anti-aircraft gun. That's what you say; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was its purpose? If we listen to what another witness said here, he sold us that the SRK had no planes. So this ABiH gun, what was its purpose? Do you have any idea? I mean, you were there in the field.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose of the anti-aircraft gun was to destroy vehicles that were moving along that road, and the people in the vehicles, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we tender this document as a Defence exhibit, please. This photograph, rather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will be admitted, and we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to look at another photograph. I would like to deal with photograph C11, page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, do you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now because we looked at the hill that you pointed to, to the extreme right, can you now indicate the line of the positions of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina on this photograph, and you can mark it from one end of the photograph to the other.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with the letter "A", please.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And if you can also please tell us the ridge that we're talking about and refer to as Grdonj, what was the name of that ridge in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: If you're talking about this rock that we refer to as a ridge, to tell you the truth, I don't think that it had a name at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please also save this photograph, and I would like to tender it as an exhibit of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D321, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, and now I would like to ask you if you know when General Dragomir Milosevic assumed the position at the head of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: General Milosevic assumed the duty of the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps in August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us if you know what happened with heavy weapons in 1994, regardless of whether it was weaponry of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Based on the Security Council Resolution from 1994, I don't know exactly from which month, heavy weaponry of the army of Republika Srpska or the federation had to be pulled out 20 kilometres into the depth of the areas they had under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said about -- you spoke about an hour ago about the events in the place that is frequently referred to as Spicasta Stijena, and you said that there were almost daily clashes there. And you also mentioned September 1994 as the time when significant incident took place. Can you please tell us exactly what happened then?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In 1994 in September, I think it was the second half of the month, forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina exerted a lot of pressure on this section of positions of the army of Republika Srpska. I think the attack went on for two or three days, and I think they even captured two or three trenches, I'm not sure how many, with the objective of capturing the road and cutting the road, cutting off our forces, and to capture that part of the terrain in order to push us back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show you a document just for you to look at briefly and to see if that corresponds to what you are telling us now. This is document D156. When you have the document in front you, can you please tell us the date, and can you briefly look at paragraph 1 under item 2, to see if this is something that corresponds to this incident from September 1994. Can you please read the heading out loud and what it says in the first paragraph of item 2, under the heading "Our Forces."

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: "Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, command of the 1st Corps, date 19th of September, 1994." "At the Sarajevo front our forces, on the 18th of September, 1994, carried out active combat with the objective of capturing Spicasta Stijena and Mala Kula. For this assignment the following forces were engaged: Platoon strength from the 120th -- or from the 129th Mountain Brigade, Crni Labudovi, Black Swans; a platoon of the MUP Bosnia, a reconnaissance sabotage platoon of the 105th Mountain Brigade, the 2nd intervention platoon from the 105th Mountain Brigade, a pioneer's platoon, a platoon of engineers."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. We don't have to go into all of that. But anyway, does that correspond to the incident that you mentioned that went on for several days?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you please tell me, this was in the month of September. Did anything of significance also happen in that period, in autumn that you would be able to tell the Judges about?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I can say that forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina changed their tactics slightly in this section of the front, precisely because heavy weaponry had been pulled out to a 20-kilometre exclusion zone, and any firing along the lines of army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Sarajevo was forbidden. They pulled out some of their forces from Sarajevo and carried out a major offensive in August at the Nisici front where we lost a substantial amount of territory, and we needed a month to re-establish those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Precisely this event of the 18th and the 19th of September, 1994, happened at our section of the front. It was simultaneous coordination with the Nisici forces in order to improve their positions in our sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And this is September, and you can now tell us about October, November, December. Did anything else happen then?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: September and the first half of October at the Nisici theatre were fairly calm, we can say, but November and December had a lot of combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In that time, did you leave the positions?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what happened in two words? How did you leave your positions?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: You mean me, personally, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's not lose time on that. You said it was November, December. It was quiet.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In November and December there were activities on the Nisici front.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did this stop at some point or end at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It ended with a truce that was established on the 1st of January, 1990 -- and it officially went on until 1990 -- the 1st of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: There was a large offensive that was prepared along all the lines of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps during the truce, which happened in the early morning hours on the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember who announced this offensive in the media?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, the then president of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, publicly stated that by mid-June there would be a large offensive to destroy the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us something at the beginning of your evidence. I will take you back to that, but could you please tell us, how did this offensive that started on the 15th of June, 1995, look like?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, this offensive started -- there was pressure on all the front lines held by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps units, and the BH army forces had, during the cease-fire, obtained weapons. I don't know through which channels. And ammunition, too. So they had so much weapons and ammunition that it was by sheer luck that we managed to hold on to some very important positions for our forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I would like to deal with some other issues relating to those -- those first few days because you mentioned them an hour ago. What happened in this period between the 15th and the 20th of June?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: On the 15th and the 16th of June, 1995, the biggest success of the BH army was -- lay in the fact that they cut the Vogosca-Srednje road. They broke through our lines and entered about two kilometres into the depth of our territory. There was fierce fighting in this area, and two days later, we managed to recapture those areas and re-establish the lines at the positions where they were before the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are those positions where you were, Grdonj and this road leading to Vogosca and Pale, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, they launched a very fierce offensive there, too, because they must have had really good coordination. When they broke through to the lines and cut this stretch of the road, Vogosca-Srednje road, the BH army forces that were -- I think it was the 105th or 109th, they tried to cut this road at Mrkovici to link up with the forces that had cut the road at this other position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me show you a document. That's DD003046. The transcript is -- does not reflect the correct number that I asked for. It's DD003046.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this doesn't have a translation, but could I perhaps read a couple of things from this document to show them to this witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, if they are short passages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To make it as fast as possible, could I just read it very briefly so that the witness then can -- so that things go on faster?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, this is about a document from the BH army. The date is the 18th of June, and item 1.2 reads: "On the Pale-Vogosca road," this is information about the enemy, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, "there has been an increase in the number of luxury cars and trucks moving at large -- large distance between them." Then it goes on: "Information about our own forces. Our forces fired from an anti-aircraft gun on the vehicles moving along the Mrkovici-Vogosca road at 1800 hours and at 2200 hours. Those vehicles were targeted by 82-millimetre mortars." Does this correspond to what you just told us about the events at Vogosca-Pale road where those luxury vehicles and trucks were moving?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This corresponds to this report, because as I already said when the Vogosca-Srednje road was cut after the two days of fighting to recapture this -- these positions, the people were moved out of this area. They moved to Pale. And those were the vehicles that were targeted as described in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit. I would like to have it marked for identification until we obtain a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll mark this for identification as D322.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before I show you another document, and that should be the end of it, in those days up until the 20th, so between the 15th and the 20th, were there any casualties in this fighting? Well, here a mention is made of mortars. So were there any casualties among the soldiers and the civilians in this area where you were?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In those operations, in both actions, in the four days we lost 32 fighters, and I don't know how many people were wounded. And I know that there were civilian casualties too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In this column of refugees that was heading down the road that we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I'm telling you when I talk about civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And let me show you this document. This was on the 18th of June, and I will now show you a document, DD003048. It's a Defence exhibit marked for identification. According to my records, it's D313 MFI. It was tendered a couple of days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may proceed in the same manner to speed up our work. This is a document that's already been marked for identification as a Defence exhibit. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will read slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And to let you know that you are now beyond the time that was allotted to you of one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was mindful of that, and I will -- this will be my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So this is a document dated the 20th of June, 1995, the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, regular combat report. "Information about our own forces." Item 2.1: "At 1800 hours our forces carried out an attack from a distance on the p/k l/o of the enemy. Anti-armour weapons were used to target the trench at the Spicasta Stijena, Krstaseva Kuca, the trench below the crossroads of the Barice-Mrkovici road and Mala Kula. On that occasion, the trenches at the Spicasta Stijena, Mala Kula and Krstaseva Kuca suffered a direct hit. The effect of those attacks is excellent." Does this correspond to what happened two days after the events that you described just now?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question. In addition to this road that was constantly targeted, do you have any information about any other points or roads that were targeted in the same way as this road at Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The Lukavica-Trebevic-Pale road was targeted in the same manner as this road that we were at.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At what point?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, Zlatiste was particularly targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: My name is Manoj Sachdeva, and I'm a lawyer for the Prosecution, and I'm going to be asking you some questions. Can I just start with getting some -- some background details? You were in the Kosevo Battalion, as I understand -- or the Kosevo Brigade from the onset of the conflict through to the end of the war. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you gave evidence that in early 1994, the Kosevo Brigade was amalgamated with the -- well, was actually subsumed within the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when it became the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, so we're talking 1994, 1995, you gave evidence that you were a battalion commander, the 1st Battalion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I think that this is not what I said. The order of things is wrong. It's the other way around. I said when the Kosevo Brigade was established, I was the commander of the 2nd Battalion in the Kosevo Brigade. That was until the spring of 1994, or from spring of 1994 until the establishment of the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. And I recall that when the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade was established, you were the commander of the 1st Battalion within that brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So what were you doing in the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, as I indicated at the start, I was one of the operations officers. I was the assistant to the chief of staff for operations and training, and it was my task to deal with the lines held by the Republika Srpska army at Mrkovic and Vogosca. So I was there when -- while I was in the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And who was, at the time, your chief or your supervisor? In other words, the chief of staff for operations and training within the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The chief of staff in the Sarajevo Brigade was Major Miro Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And at that time the commander of the brigade was Dragan Josipovic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where were your brigade headquarters? Where were the brigade headquarters for the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in your role as the assistant to the chief of staff for operations and training, from 1994 through to 1995, approximately how -- how much of the time was spent in the command headquarters? How much time did you spend at the command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I spent very little time at the headquarters of the brigade. I mostly did my job in the field, except on those days when there were no major combat operations and when I had my regular duty days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you were at the command headquarters did you participate in regular meetings with other members of the command and indeed the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: At those regular meetings or briefings, as we used to call them, at the brigade there would always be one of the assistants to the chief of staff for operations in training, but on most occasions it would be the one who was on duty in the command headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: There would always be someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So I take it that you did attend some of those meetings.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And at those meetings, presumably your department, in other words, the department for operations and training, would brief the brigade commander about the previous day's activities, the forthcoming activities related to your -- to your section; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it quite like that, because all the activities that were going on or were supposed to go on, the biggest responsibility was in the hands of the commander, Dragan Josipovic. If any preparations had to be carried out for anything, that was within the purview of the duty officer in the command of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. I actually wasn't speaking about the preparations, but let's -- let's try and do this another way. At those regular meetings that you on occasion attended, presumably there would be your unit, there would be the unit, for example, for morale and religious affairs. There may have been a logistics unit. There may have been a communications unit. And I'm simply asking that at those meetings, of course, I understand that the brigade commander makes the ultimate decision, but at those meetings each unit would have the responsibility to brief the commander as to the previous day's activities and possibly any other future activities. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So at least within the -- within your remit, within the remit of your unit, you would brief the brigade commander and other persons in the hierarchy of issues related to training, issues related to the workings of the operations department.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Not I, personally, but through the chief of staff. The chief of staff had us as his assistants, but he submitted his reports to the brigade commander. So this was not our task to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And similarly, if the brigade commander had orders or -- well, I would say orders to the respective departments within his brigade at those meetings those orders would be -- would be given to his sections. That would be the -- the format in which it was done; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, all the tasks were agreed at the meetings. Every unit would get not only oral orders but also written orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the oral orders would -- would be communicated through, I understand, induction telephones and other means; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Not always. In fact, very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So how were -- how were the oral orders communicated in?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Oral orders were communicated personally. In person, in other words. Because of the audio surveillance carried out by the enemy forces telephones were seldom used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you spoke just before you completed your -- completed the examination-in-chief you spoke about a Security Council Resolution with respect to heavy weapons. Do you remember speaking about that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it that you -- you and your fellow colleagues within the command became aware of these -- of this Security Council Resolution at those meetings, or was there another way that you became aware of this Security Council Resolution?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: We knew that before, but we were notified officially from the command, the corps command. But reports had already appeared in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And because this Security Council Resolution related to the -- to the two warring factions, I take it that other Security Council Resolutions that also related to the ABiH, to the SRK, the contents of those Security Council Resolutions would have been communicated to -- to the brigades, to the brigade staff. Is that a fair statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'll try again. You've told us that the Security Council Resolution that you spoke about with respect to the heavy weapons, you became aware of that. Do you remember telling the Court that? You said that you were notified officially from the command, from the corps command.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was a Resolution or an order. You can call it whatever you wish, but we learned about this Resolution or order because there had been debate about it for maybe 20 days or a month before this decision was actually taken to withdraw the heavy weapons 20 kilometres into the depth of the territory. So everybody knew that something was going on regarding this issue. Even the small children knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm actually using your words. You said Security Council Resolution. So what I'm asking you is that -- that if there were or when there were other Security Council Resolutions or orders from the corps command that related to -- to the workings of the brigade, the brigade staff would have been aware of them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I spoke a moment ago about the -- the different units that may have been at these meetings that you attended on occasion, and I spoke about the department for logistics, and I also spoke about a unit of the department for morale and religious affairs. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And at the time -- at the time you were within the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, in other words, at the time you were the assistant to the chief of staff for training and operations, I understand that the commander for morale and religious affairs was somebody called Miroslav Krajisnik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, sir, is it also correct that while he had this -- this role within that unit, he also was -- how should I put it? He was a liaison officer or he was involved in cooperation with the UNPROFOR; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: For a time, yes, but as to how long we had this member of our brigade who was a liaison with UNPROFOR I can't tell you, but the answer is yes, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And I shall get back to that in a moment. Can I ask you, you remember being asked questions about the -- about the sniping -- the training for snipers? Do you remember those questions by His Honour Judge Mindua?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said -- you said that -- in one of the answers you said, "I can't tell you that I saw this because I didn't, but I think that because it was winter this order could not be carried out and this is why the commander did not issue an order to carry out this order that had been sent down from the corps." Do you remember your answer to His Honour Judge Mindua?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
