utterances.text: Now, leaving aside whether you actually saw this -- this order or whether you actually went for the training, you knew, because you were an assistant to the commander for training and operations, you knew that you had been selected as one of these trainers for a sniper course. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document, sir. If I could ask for -- it's P682 or 762. For some reason it was tendered twice. Now, sir, you see on the screen that this document is dated the 15th of January, 1995. And if we can please go -- I'm sorry, I'm going to have to go back and forth, but if we go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, are you saying something? No? No. You're just exercising. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can the last page be scrolled down, please, to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you see on the right-hand side you see that it is -- it's -- it comes from your commander of the brigade, Dragan Josipovic. Do you see that there, sir? Yes, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you're -- you remember seeing at the front that this was a document from the command of the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, in other words, the corps command. Do you remember seeing that or do you want me to show that to you again?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: If it's not a problem, could you please turn to that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could go to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You see there it emanates from the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, and you'll see on the right-hand side the command of the SRK. You see that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the order dated the 5th of January, 1995, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, if we could move to the -- it's the third page in the -- in the Serbian version and the -- and the fourth page in the English. Now, sir, you'll see in the middle of the document, in the middle of the page or on the Serbian version it's down towards the bottom, you'll see a list of names and I take it you see your name there. Lieutenant Vlajko Bozic.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry for my pronunciation. That's your name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you see that there was -- there is a recommendation sent to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps for -- for you to be sent for training instructor's course. You see that's what it says, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you see below that there are six persons that are selected for sniper training also.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you also see that at the bottom, the line at the bottom of the second list of names that Lukavica is recommended as a site for the training. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Could you please show me that? Where is this? Okay. Yeah. Fine, fine. Yes, I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: You may not have gone to Jahorina, but did you go to Lukavica for training?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Lukavica for training?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But are you still maintaining your evidence that you were not aware that you had been chosen to be an instructor? Is that still your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I remember this document from our unit, but I never went to this instructor's course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And now that you remember this document, your answer you gave me previously that you don't or you were not aware that you had been selected, that must cause you to -- to reflect on your answer. So you were aware that you had been chosen to go on this course. Leaving aside whether you went or not, but you were aware that you had been chosen. Isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: If you are referring to the list that was shown by Mr. Tapuskovic and this list, I think that we're talking about two different lists that served two different purposes. In the initial situation -- in the initial situation, it says that I am appointed to conduct a course, sniper's course. That's in the first document that was offered by Mr. Tapuskovic, and on -- in this document that you're talking about, my name is put forward to attend the instructor's course. So according to me, we're talking about two different documents, two different purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. So you were, nevertheless, aware that you had been selected to attend the instructor's course for sniping. You're aware of that, aren't you? You may not have gone, but you were aware that you had been selected. Just answer the question yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say here the course for the instructors who will then carry out sniper training, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that -- were you aware that you had been selected for training -- for a training instructor's course? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Incidentally, do you -- these names, the five, six names at the bottom, Miroslavko Ivetic, Slavko Peric, Aleksandar Jokic, Zoran Sucur, do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: They were snipers, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your brigade, the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade did have didn't it, a sniping platoon or a sniping unit, in addition to the infantry soldiers that it had; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to move on now. Now, you spoke about the media earlier in your examination-in-chief and also a little bit with me. You remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that -- well, let me ask you this: Did you have available to you and did the brigade have available to it the -- the media from the federation side, let's say the ABiH side, in addition to the media from the VRS side, from the Bosnian Serb side?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it, then, that when you or your fellow soldiers would be listening -- sorry, was it radio and television or one or the other or was it both?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: We could listen to the radio, and the only TV channel that we got from Sarajevo was Hayat TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So with the radio and the television channel, you must have been aware of what the federation side and the VRS side were reporting in terms of how the conflict was progressing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And see, sir, I take it when -- on the occasions when you were to watch the media of the federation or listen to the radio of the federation, in other words, the ABiH, you must have been aware of the - how should it put it? - the allegations that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps forces were shelling and sniping at civilians in the city. You must have heard those stories; right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And presumably you also must have heard from the Sarajevo -- from the Bosnian Serb side you probably must have heard that the stories that were coming out of the Bosnian federation side were -- allegations were false, were propaganda. That also must have been something that you heard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, at these meetings that you attended, the meetings at the brigade command, were these allegations of the shelling and sniping of civilians by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps forces, were these allegations ever brought up in these meetings? Were they ever discussed?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When they were discussed, since I take it when you say seldom that they were discussed, is that a correct understanding, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Who would initiate the discussion? Would it be Dragan Josipovic himself?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when he initiated the discussion, how did it he -- how did he do that? What did he say?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I already said that those things were discussed seldom, but in most cases most of the things had to do with this decision to pull out the heavy weapons 20 kilometres into the depth of the territory because the Sarajevo side contributed to this decision being made by their false reports of the shelling incidents involving civilians, targeting civilians in the city and this led to this whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did Dragan Josipovic maintain that these were false reports?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And how was he able to establish that these were false reports?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how he was able to establish that those allegations were false, but I know that a lot of what could be seen in the media or through other channels originating from Sarajevo, I know that a lot of it was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, let me give you an example if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you a question before, before that, sir, if you don't mind. You said that you don't know how Dragan Josipovic was able to establish whether -- that they were false reports. In the meetings that you attended, did you ever hear or did Dragan Josipovic ever say -- did he ever initiate an investigation into the conduct of soldiers within his brigade with respect to these allegations?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember any such occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to move to some of the photographs that you marked. If I could ask for -- I think it's the first one, D -- D318. Sir, you remember this photograph. It looks a bit complicated, but you remember these markings?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, firstly I want to ask you, you see the hills in the background, in other words, to the top of the photograph. You see those hills at the top of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Those hills are -- well, that's Mrkovici, is it not?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Mrkovici is -- is below these hills here, so it's a part of this green surface just below the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Nevertheless, those hills that we see in the top part of the picture, during the conflict were controlled by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And it's clear, is it not, sir, that those hills are higher in elevation than Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And similarly I take it we can't see the area of Poljine in this photograph, but Poljine was also higher in elevation than Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No. Poljine, like Poljine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand that. You said Poljine was not higher than Grdonj, but then you said Poljine --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Poljine is part of a neighbourhood. That's what it's called, the Poljine neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked -- you remember you were asked to identify the -- the VRS lines, in other words the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps lines behind the ridge-line of what was termed Spicasta Stijena. Do you remember giving evidence about that? You said it was at least 50 metres below the ridge.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Behind. Not below, but behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, behind. As -- as the chief of -- as the assistant to the chief of staff for operations and training, were you ever positioned in those trenches that we -- that you've just spoken about during the period 1994 and 1995? Were you personally ever there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How many times were you there if you can tell the Court that. I appreciate it's some time ago, but if you can, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I was there throughout, during combat actions and in the critical time period when we were losing some trenches in this sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, let me just try and get some clarity. When you say you were there throughout, you don't mean that you were there for the whole of 1994 and the whole of 1995. I take it that you mean that you were there during specific -- specific combat activity. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Were you there in the -- while the combat operation of the 19th of September, 1994, took place? Were you there then, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said that these -- these VRS lines, these trenches were some -- were at least 50 metres below the ridge. The Defence has brought a previous witness who has also testified in this case, a soldier -- or shall I say someone who was also in those trenches, and his evidence was that perhaps they were some 20 to 40 metres behind the ridge. Is that a possibility, sir? Is it perhaps maybe 20 metres towards 50 to 80 metres? Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I can say with certainty that the trenches were behind the ridge, and they were at least 50 metres away. Behind the ridge. Not to the right or to the left, behind the actual ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I understand the position, sir. I'm just talking about the distance. This witness has said 20 to 40 metres, and I'm just wondering whether he may have been correct or you still maintain what you're saying. I'm talking, you know, from the top of the ridge, from the ridge-line.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Behind the top of the ridge, the way I described. Behind the top of the ridge. These two arrows that I drew on one side and the other, that is where the trenches were on the slope of the ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you're saying they were some 50 metres from the top of the ridge.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't measure it, but that would be that approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you see in the foreground or the bottom part of the picture if you look to your right, you'll see a collection of houses. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And those houses represent the village of Sedrenik, don't they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you will agree with me, sir, that from the top of the ridge there is a clear view of that part of the Sedrenik, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask you to mark the village of Sedrenik. If you can put -- if you can just place the letters "SR" at that village where the houses are on the bottom right-hand side that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The village of Sedrenik is this entire complex. Can I have the picture back again, please? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It's not a row of houses. It's the entire area, even lower down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I think I said collection of houses, but if you could just put "SR" in that black circle.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: You said a group of houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, I take it that from the -- the trenches -- the trenches that were 50 metres behind the top of the ridge you would -- or the soldiers in those trenches would not have been able to see the ABiH trenches at the -- the other side of the ridge, the bottom slope of the ridge.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say, "No," you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: You couldn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to make sure it's recorded properly on the transcript. And --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: You just asked about the ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Only the ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. And the ABiH lines that are just on the other side of the ridge, I think you said in evidence were some hundred to hundred and fifty metres from the ridge-line; that is right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The lines of the forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina were just below the ridge. But like I said at some point in one area, this area to the right that we marked with a "W", that is where there is a forested area. There it was from 150 to 200 metres apart. But below the ridge the ridge is about 50 metres high. So they were just below the ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you -- do you remember your time while you were at the trenches and also while you were within the brigade, do you remember somebody called Vaso Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Vaso Nikolic? Yes, I think that I do remember. I knew a man named Vaso. I'm not sure if his last name was Nikolic, though, but I think that I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did you know him from -- from being stationed at the trenches behind the ridge?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In any case, he -- he was a soldier with the Sarajevo -- 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, and he was stationed behind the trenches, and -- well, let me just ask you this: While it's correct that there were no permanent positions on top of the ridge either by the SRK --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- You asked him whether he knew him from being stationed at the trenches behind the ridge and he said no, and then you put a question, "In any case, he was a soldier with the Sarajevo Brigade, and he was stationed behind the trenches." But isn't that what he just said no to?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. President. However, I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, you are putting --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're putting that to him that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm going to put it again to him when I get to that part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, my question was -- my next question is this: That there were no -- on top of the ridge, in other words, on the ridge-line itself is it correct that there were no SRK positions there, permanent positions there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: They were not temporary or permanent positions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, of course, the ABiH were never on top of that ridge, were they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, is it not correct, however, that from the trenches behind the ridge-line there was -- the soldiers of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps could, as it were, crawl up to the ridge where there would be a small observation point on top of that ridge?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This perhaps could have happened in 1992, but later the ridge was mined from our side and their side. So it was not possible for anybody to go up to the ridge and do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm talking about the -- presumably if you're stationed at your trenches behind the ridge, if you look up, up towards the slope, you would see the top of the ridge, is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I still put to you, sir, that on the top of the ridge, maybe just beneath the rim of the ridge, there was a small observation point where a SRK soldier could take a commanding view of the village at Sedrenik and also the ABiH lines. Do you agree with that or not, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has just said that from -- that in 1992, it could have been a surveillance point, but after 1992, because those places were mined by both sides, after 1992 it was not possible, like he said, like he explained earlier, that it was impossible to get up to that elevation, the point on the ridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That may be so, Mr. Tapuskovic, but Mr. Sachdeva has different instructions, and he's entitled to put his case to the witness on the basis of his instructions. That's what cross-examination is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps I can ask you another way. Maybe -- maybe it will be -- it will be more clear for you. The gentleman that we spoke about, Mr. Nikolic, he testified in -- in this institution in the Galic case, and he gave evidence, as you are doing, under oath that there was an observation point on top of the ridge where, of course, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps soldiers would -- they would go there and use that observation point to -- to conduct surveillance or to observe what was happening in enemy territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, then it would be necessary to state the time period that the witness Nikolic was talking about. When was this precisely, so that the witness here could fully answer. What was the time period that the witness Nikolic from the Galic case referred to in this matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, are you in a position to give the time period?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President, and I understood that I indeed said that in my question. Perhaps the interpretation -- but I remember specifically saying that throughout the conflict. In other words, 1992 to 1995. In any case, that's the time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bozic, Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Galic case I know and I read it, it was not permitted to put questions outside of the time period relevant to Mr. Galic. So if it's a question whether this was possible throughout the entire period, I don't think we can do it like that unless we find it in the transcript that it says like that, because I know that in the Galic case the latest date that some activities could be discussed, the cut-off date, would be the 10th of August, 1995 -- no, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, are you putting it to him on the basis of what Nikolic said in the Galic case? Because if you are, then you have to be faithful to the -- to what was said in the Galic case. But do we have a transcript of what was said in the Galic case indicating the time period?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I just have a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tapuskovic, you should have a copy of this transcript. I understand this was given to you last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. I already said that, Your Honours. I am not able to think every time I'm expecting a witness, especially not when we're talking about the presentation of evidence of the Prosecution and the presentation of evidence of us, to pay attention to the Galic witnesses in that time period that pertains to that case. I always concentrated on the time period relevant to Dragomir Milosevic. I was not able to deal with things that require a vast amount of time. We still don't know which time period should this case be dealing with definitely, I mean in relation to the adjudicated facts. I really did not think about that, nor was I -- was that something that I was dealing with over the past few days because of the large number of work that I had to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, if you can't identify the time period referred to by Nikolic in the Galic case, then I won't permit you to put the question. You have to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will find the citation. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps you can come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness -- Mr. Bozic, may just ask you to -- to answer the question that in 1994/1995, are you aware of an observation point on top of the ridge that was used by SRK soldiers? And I'm only suggesting that it was used for observation purposes at this stage.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I just said at that time in 1994, 1995, 1993, this place could not be used as an observation point because it was mined. So if anyone managed to get up there would not -- they would not come back alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: The -- the -- if you're looking up from the trenches and you're looking up to the ridge, in other words, from the VRS trenches -- just imagine yourself doing that.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that that -- that area between the -- the area between where you are and where the ridge is was mined by the SRK? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It was mined both by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and by the army of Republika Srpska. Let me clarify. This is not just a simple ridge. It has a plateau that is about 10 metres wide at some points, and it's at a mild upward slope. It's not just the edge and a ridge. There is space there for people to get up there in order to get to the beginning or the top of the ridge from where they could see the area of Sedrenik, they would need to cross some 10 metres in certain places. In relation to the forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the left and the right side, this was not possible to do even if the terrain was not mined. So it's not just a simple ridge. It's not just a sharp edge. It's a rock that has its length and width.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying that the plateau was mined?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And so which soldiers did that, the SRK soldiers or the ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He said both.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, he said both, but I want to establish in particular which area, because --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, what could be seen from our side, from our side behind the ridge was mined by the army of Republika Srpska. The sides of the ridge and up to the top of the ridge were mined by fighters of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, that's what I'm asking you. The slopes leading up to the top of the ridge were mined by your soldiers. That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: From our side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what about the plateau? What about the top of the ridge?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain that. This ridge did not have a peak. It's a plateau some 10 metres, more or less, wide. So it doesn't have a literal peak, a summit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, I asked you about the plateau. A simple question. Was the plateau mined?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The plateau was mined by the army of Republika Srpska in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So what you're telling the Court is that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina personnel would go up the slope on top of the ridge, on the plateau and expose themselves and lay mines. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: That's not what I said. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He said that -- he said the plateau was mined by the army of Republika Srpska in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No, he said the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. President. At least that's what the transcript said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. No, he said -- the answer at line 21: "The plateau was mined by the army of Republika Srpska in the beginning."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I apologise. That was inadvertent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So I take it if the SRK mined this area, they obviously knew where the mines were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that they didn't know about all the mines, because at the beginning, as I already said in answer to Mr. Tapuskovic's question, the units that were there, the people in those units did not have -- they were not organised into units. So everybody laid mines as they saw fit in order to prevent the BH army forces from pouring over the ridge. So they could have known about some mines but not all of them, and that's why I can really vouch for them never going into that plateau at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, did you yourself lay mines on that ridge?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it you weren't there in 1992 when the mines were laid, were you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And how do you know that mines were laid there?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that. I heard that from the fighters who laid the mines. So from the stories told to me by those soldiers who laid down those mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So your evidence is that mines would be laid in Sarajevo-Romanija Corps territory, but that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps soldiers would not really know where those mines were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't understand that -- that's his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's what -- that's, in my submission, what the witness said, Mr. President, that -- that these mines were laid by -- by the Serb forces in the beginning, but they weren't -- people did not know or the soldiers did not know where all these mines were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's your answer to that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer to this is as follows: When I said that we were not organised, I meant that these people had not been trained to lay minefields, proper minefields, so they laid mines without making any protocols that could be used later to determine where those mines were laid. And since in those trenches -- the trenches were not always manned by the same people, they took shifts, 24-hour, 48-hour, 7-day shifts, it would happen that several people would lay mines in that part of the terrain. That's why I said people knew about some mines but didn't know about other mines. So not all the people there knew about all the mines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, we're going to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva. You're having technical problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, before we broke you were saying that -- that according to your knowledge, although you weren't there, these mines were laid in 1992, at the beginning of the conflict; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In 1992. I don't know whether it was in the beginning or later, but it was definitely that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And so when we spoke about Mr. Nikolic who was a soldier with the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade, and when he spoke or gave evidence under oath about an observation point on the ridge or very close to the ridge itself in 1993 and 1994, he either would have had to negotiate the mines or knew where the mines were or in fact the mines were not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When my learned friend Mr. Sachdeva put the question, Your Honours, he said "close to the ridge or on the ridge itself." So is it near the ridge or on the ridge? This has to be specified. Mr. Sachdeva said that the observation point was placed close to the ridge or on the ridge, and it's important to be certain about what the witness said. Was it on the ridge or close to the ridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'll reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, what I'm suggesting to you is that Mr. Nikolic testified that in 1993 and 1994, there was a position, an observation position, a surveillance position, on the ridge or at least located on the ridge that would permit SRK troops to look down onto the village of Sedrenik. That's the evidence the witness gave, and what I'm asking you now, that either he must have been able to negotiate the mines that you say were laid, or in fact, there indeed were no mines that prevented the soldiers from coming up to the ridge. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Let me just say one thing regarding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. When counsel is on his feet, you have to stop speaking. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. It's fine that my learned colleague Mr. Sachdeva is insisting on it and confronting the witness with this testimony, but perhaps he could give us a page reference so that we could respond to it. What page of the transcript is this part of the evidence referred to by Mr. Sachdeva?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva, what's the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It's the transcript page 16067.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Excuse me. 16067, 16045, on the 21st of November, 2002. And indeed -- indeed it is also mentioned in paragraph 511 of the Galic judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you were about to answer the question, or do you need me to -- to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No. There's no need. This ridge, this is sheer rock. It is impossible to set up any observation post there even had not this terrain been mined. I know that this was mined, however, and I know that there was no observation post at this plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You know that they were -- you know that it was not -- you know that it was mined because you were told stories about that. You weren't there when it was allegedly mined, were you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I have one second to confer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could ask for Defence Exhibit 319 to be shown. I believe that's the second photograph. And if I could have a moment to fix my headphones I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you remember this photograph that you marked?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you remember those two arrows you have drawn coming up from the -- the lines that you have marked as ABiH lines, those two arrows?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And those arrows indicate where a gully or a -- well, I'll use the word "gully" because I think that's what counsel for the Defence used. Those arrows depict or they indicate where the gully was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask you to take a pen and just put a "G" by both those arrows, please.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask for this photograph to be admitted as a Prosecution exhibit with the new markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What does it show that is not already there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I would like to explain that. However, with your leave, I would like to explain that in a manner that the -- that the witness does not hear. So perhaps I could ask for the witness to take off his headphones and I can explain that to you, why I ask the specific question. I would be happy to, but I wouldn't want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We will all wait in suspense, so please go ahead and put the question or -- just go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You want me to go ahead and explain to you or to carry on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Has the -- can I ask for a number to be given to the photograph if it hasn't been done already?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll admit that as P908.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's already been admitted into evidence, but we should have continued with the questions, because we have to see why those two positions are marked. I can't see the purpose of those two marks that were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We have ruled on the matter, Mr. Tapuskovic, and we have allowed the Prosecution to -- to go ahead. And as I said, we will all wait with suspense to what comes out of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked -- answering questions about the -- the combat operation on the 19th of September, 1994. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you testified that you were yourself involved in that operation.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Incidentally, what types of weapons did you personally have when you were involved in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what type was that please?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It was an M-72 automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you remember that Mr. Tapuskovic showed you a document from the ABiH, and you confirmed the contents of that document. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could ask for D156 to be -- to be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, the first thing I want to draw your attention to is that if we look at the -- the text under item 2 which says "Nase snege," "Our Forces." And it's right is it not, sir, that at the bottom of the page it states that while there may have -- it states and I'm summarising, while there may have been combat activity on that date, in the end the Sarajevo-Romanija forces retook the part of Spicasta Stijena that they lost during the day. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, in fact, do you remember giving evidence yourself that, I think you said, within a couple of days it was retaken by the Serb forces. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I said that we had lost two or three trenches in that stretch that we held, but I hadn't said that we had lost the ridge or that the BH forces had taken the ridge. On the map that I was shown last, before this document, that is why I made those two lines that marked those passages, those passes to the left and to the right of the Spicasta Stijena, and those two trenches were taken by the BH army. They did not take Spicasta Stijena. The Spicasta Stijena area is a little bit broader.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't say Spicasta Stijena. I said a part of Spicasta Stijena. In any case, the parts that were taken -- the parts that were taken by the ABiH on that day were retaken, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, told the Court that, that's at least in the trenches or in that area, there were only infantry weapons, that you only had infantry weapons. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But nevertheless at least in this operation, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps did indeed draw upon artillery support. In other words, 80 to 122-millimetre mortars to retake or to fight in that combat operation. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The 80-millimetre mortars were used, but as for the 120-millimetre mortars, those were among the weapons that had to be withdrawn 20 kilometres into the depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, we'll move into that in a moment, but you will see in the text here that it refers to the use by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of 80 -- well, 60-millimetre mortars, 82-millimetre mortars, and 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: That's what they say. That's what they write.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you have --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: That's their report and that's what it says there. I'm telling you what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But you just confirmed -- you have confirmed -- you have confirmed this report in your evidence-in-chief, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I confirmed the report along the lines that I was asked -- that Mr. Tapuskovic asked me about the attack, about the date, and I confirmed that the attack really did take place on that date, and in this sense I confirmed the accuracy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But you agree that in this operation 82-millimetre mortars were used, and 60-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that in your time in the JNA you were with an anti-tank platoon. You were a gunnery -- or you were involved in the gunnery department; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: While I was in the Yugoslav People's Army, I was in the infantry. I was not in the armoured units, I was in infantry. Plain and simple. As far as I know, the 60- and 82-millimetre mortars were weapons used by the infantry, just plain infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, sir, isn't it correct that in 1992, you indeed were an assistant gunner in the JNA in an anti-tank platoon in Donja Dubica?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In Donja Dubica. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Nevertheless, sir, you know that an 82-millimetre mortar, with the charges that can be placed on such a mortar, may -- has possibly a maximum range of three to four kilometres. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you also know that the heavy weapons exclusion zone agreement strictly prohibited the use of 82-millimetre mortars. They came under the heavy weapons exclusion zone, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I am not sure that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Nevertheless, in September 1994, the SRK deployed 82-millimetre mortars. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: 82-millimetre mortars, we had them. I don't know whether they had been moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that -- I suggest to you that they were not moved out.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, they were not moved out. I said that I -- we had 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, with respect -- and I'm sticking on to -- to weaponry. As you've said to the Court, you were -- you were the assistant to the commander of operations in training; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it that your job was to assist -- well, in assisting the operations commander, you would be -- you would plan with him how to effect or how to implement combat operations that the brigade commander would -- would decide upon. Is that a clear enough question, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The question is clear, but what you're putting to me is not accurate, not in the form that you just put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: The brigade commander would suggest a course of action, a course of combat action, and your job or your unit's job was to ensure the best and most efficient way for that action to take place. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No. What you're saying, it could apply had we carried out offensive actions, but since our forces carried out only defensive actions we couldn't have foreseen any situation that would arise out of actions by the BH army and then plan our response. We could only carry out work to strengthen our positions, and we were not in a position to carry out any offensives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, sir, are you saying to the Court that when there were combat operations, whether initiated by the ABiH, in other words, the SRK had to respond, the brigade commander would not task his operations unit to devise the most efficient way to defend the territory? That must have happened, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Precisely. But the orders were very brief. Let me just tell you what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you allow me to finish, sir. So in deciding, or at least for your unit to decide upon how best to defend the territory, it would be incumbent upon the operations -- it would be --

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- Incumbent upon the operations manager to have knowledge of the weapons and ammunition at the brigade's disposal. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you another document, but before I do that let me ask you a question. In your time at the 3rd -- in the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade in your role, and, you know, you've spoken about mortars and other weapons, you must have heard about the deployment or the existence of modified air bombs within your brigade.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What does it mean modified bomb?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm speaking about a weapon called Fugasna Avio Bomba, modified air bomb. Have you ever heard of those weapons before?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I did hear about air bombs. I didn't hear about modified air bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Have you heard of the term F-A-B, FAB, 250-kilogrammes FAB, 150-kilogrammes. Did you ever see that in documents, did you ever hear about that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify what does it mean, FAB?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, firstly, can you answer the question? Did you ever hear of the term FAB or did you ever see it written down FAB 250, FAB 105?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I may have heard that term. I don't think so, but at any rate I never saw it written down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you -- you said you may have heard of that term. I suggest to you and would you agree with my suggestion that the FAB stands for and please excuse my pronunciation, but Fugasna Avio Bomba?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I heard about this term Fugasna Avio Bomba.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Fugasna Avio Bomba. And when you say you heard about this term, I take it you heard about this term and this term for this weapon during your time at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: While I was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you were in the brigade you were in the army, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: That's what it looks like now, but it was a little bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you a document. If I could ask for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean by the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say the word "army," "armija," I'm referring to the regular army of a state that is garrisoned in barracks and where people work as soldiers. This is the regular army of a state. I'm talking about professional soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness misunderstood. Of course, your intervention is very apropos, but perhaps the witness should explain which army he had in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer about where I had heard about FAB, I meant that I had heard it when I was doing my national service in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The JNA, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I may ask for -- if I may ask for Prosecution Exhibit 761 to be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What years were that, Witness, when you were doing your national service in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1985.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you've heard about FABs, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bozic, you'll see a document on your screen, and it is a document from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command. Do you see that there? On the 17th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And it's signed by Cedo Sladoje who was the chief of staff at the time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you'll see there that it says that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command is ordering the delivery of three pieces FAB 105 kg, two pieces FAB 250 kg, ordering for those supplies to be given to the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade. You see, at least that's what it says there, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And with this document on your screen and with this information, and in your role within the operations department or the operations unit of your brigade command, is it still your evidence that at any time during the period 1994 to 1995 you did not hear about the existence, the use, the deployment of these FAB bombs?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: You said in 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. You can -- you can focus on those years, but in fact I will ask you from 1992 to 1995. In other words, during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Those are air bombs. So as far as I know, our units did not have any aircraft, and these bombs are used by the aircraft. I really can't see how those bombs could be used at all. So everything that's written here in this text looks ridiculous to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So you're saying what has emanated from the Sarajevo Corps command, from the chief of staff, is ridiculous. That's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It's not ridiculous, but it's strange. I can't see anyway in which they could be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, sir, they could be modified, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, you didn't explain that to me, what modified means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- perhaps I will, then. What I suggest to you is this, sir, that these bombs, as you say, are designed to be dropped from aeroplanes, and as you say, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps did not have aeroplanes. We agree on that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: However, during the period -- during the conflict, and in particular during 1994 and 1995, these bombs were modified in a way that would enable them to be launched with rockets and fired from the ground.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I can state that I never saw such a bomb. I cannot say that this document is not true, but I did not see such bombs, and where I was during the war in 1992 to 1995, I don't know about such bombs being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I appreciate that you did not see such a bomb, and I appreciate also that you don't know that such bombs were used, but what I'm asking you is whether you were aware or whether you heard that these bombs existed within your brigade.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This document is probably true, but I did not hear that there were bombs in the brigade. I don't know if they ever reached there as it says on this -- in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In your time at the operations unit, did you ever see a document stating that the delivery was not successful? Did you ever see such a document, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, before I -- I'm going to conclude very shortly. You remember earlier on in the cross-examination we spoke about the meetings you attended in the brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you remember that we spoke about a one Miroslav Krajisnik who was the commander for religious and morale affairs?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you also remember that to your knowledge -- you remember that to your knowledge for some point in time while you were at the brigade, he was responsible for liaison -- liaising with UNPROFOR. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the information that was discussed at these meetings with respect to the allegations from the media about sniping and shelling civilians in Sarajevo -- you remember we discussed that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did Mr. Krajisnik in those meetings that you were present or indeed if you had -- if you have heard about those meetings where you weren't there, did he ever bring up the issue of protests by UNPROFOR about the shelling and sniping of civilians by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Perhaps I wasn't present at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me -- let me just try and probe you a bit further. You say you cannot remember, but try and think carefully. Was -- was there a time where it may have been mentioned, where it might have been mentioned? Firstly, while you were at the meetings; and secondly, whether you discussed it with colleagues after the meetings when you weren't present?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I cannot tell you if I did hear or didn't. I really cannot say. The question is not that clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, in your brigade and also -- well, in your brigade were there any specific orders or instructions in place about the way soldiers had to engage their targets, or in other words, when and how to open fire? Maybe we can categorise these instructions as rules of engagement. Did you receive such orders or do you know of such orders being rendered and delivered?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm whether these orders were in written form, but there were certainly oral orders that it was permissible to fire at strictly military targets. No firing at civilians or at facilities, buildings that were not military facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you say that it was permissible to fire at strictly military targets, that is indeed what -- what the soldiers -- what you did, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm saying that's what you did. You did fire at military targets.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And so if you were in a position with your gun and you had an ABiH soldier in your sight, you would take him out, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And so therefore, sir, it's correct that that would not be categorised as a defensive operation, would it?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: It's war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might I have one second to confer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're seven minutes over the time now, so you must conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I have two more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, just one last question on this topic. When you -- when you said it was war, did you consider that able-bodied men between the ages of 20 and 60 were legitimate targets? Did you shoot at those persons?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: All those people in the age range that you mentioned, from 20 to 60, if they were soldiers they would be in uniform with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Would you shoot a soldier who was not armed?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And lastly, sir, you spoke about the verbal orders that you received with respect to firing at military targets. I take it that those orders remained -- or the content of those orders and the meaning of those orders remained constant from 1992 through to 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: They were always in force, but I don't know if it was always possible to control or check a hundred per cent on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So you're saying that it was possible that people, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps soldiers, would indeed fire at civilians. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying that, but I say that you could not have a hundred per cent control of the action of the soldiers from the trenches at the lines of -- or the trenches of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, a while ago we admitted document P908, which was the photo with the two gullies, and we did so under the condition that you would show to us a very good reason to have this photo admitted into evidence. I realise that we have heard no such thing, and my proposal is that we delete Exhibit P908 from the files. I don't know if that is possible, and I need to consult with my colleagues, but I feel a bit deceived that we allowed you to go along with it and then you didn't deliver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, I offered to make submissions as to why I was doing that, and I didn't refer to questions that I'm going to put to the witness. I had a very specific reason as to why I did that, and I wanted to -- I wanted to inform Your Honours. However, at the time -- at the time of the examination, I wanted to do it so that the witness did not hear, but I'm very happy to -- I'm very happy to explain the purpose behind my markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we'll eliminate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, in your cross-examination, in answer to a question you said that you could provide an example of media reports being false. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to hear one example.

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say the following: Mr. Silajdzic claimed during the war in 1994 and 1995, and he said this in many places, that during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina over 200.000 people were killed, 200.000 Bosniaks. And now we have a situation that the investigation centre, in relation to all of the killed in Bosnia and Herzegovina, so I'm talking about Bosniaks, Serbs, Muslims, and other ethnic groups, came to a figure, and it's hard to speak about people who were killed as numbers, but they came to the number of 100.000, 100.000. And the head of that centre for investigations is a Bosniak. So what I want to say is that this is a substantial lie by a person who was the Minister for Foreign Affairs of his country. He said that throughout the war or in the war 200.000 Bosniaks were killed in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now the number is given which is much less and includes all of the people who were killed. So this is just an indication of information about the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, earlier on when we talked about FABs, I didn't want to go on because I didn't want to upset the cross-examination. Would you please tell me what exactly this expression FAB means, because you heard about that in the JNA. What is exactly a FAB?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did hear of that term, but I really couldn't give you a correct answer, and that is why I put the question to the Prosecutor, to clarify what FAB, F-A-B, means. I know it's a type of an air bomb, but what kind I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know whether the JNA used that type of bomb?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm -- I apologise for rising, but I -- I would -- because -- I would like to explain why I asked those questions, because I -- it was not at all my intention or the Prosecution's intention to enter into any sort of deception, so I would like to explain, and there was a very -- in my submission, there was a very legitimate reason why I asked those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you are entitled to give the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When -- when counsel for Defence asked the witness to mark the ABiH lines, he did so with the line going underneath the photograph, and then the counsel asked about the -- the geographical features, the gullies or the indentations and they were marked. And I simply wanted that -- those gullies to be marked as distinct from the ABiH lines, because that's not what, in my submission, the witness answered to and that's the reason why -- that's the reason why I had it done that way, so it would not be mixed up with the ABiH lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, we accept the explanation, and there's no -- no question at all or doubt about your integrity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just briefly like to go back, because in any case, we cannot have a new witness today, although there are 10 minutes left, but this next witness has protective measures, so we would need time to prepare. I didn't even want to put any questions, but we do have some time available, so I might as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, that is not the basis on which court time is to be used. You must have proper, relevant questions. We're not going to accommodate padding to make up time. If you don't have any questions, you don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps I was not quite precise when I said this, and I did have a document here. It's document P671. I would like to look at it again. I would have two questions to put to the witness on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has to do with the bombs, and the document. First of all, did he ever see that document? Did he ever see a written document of similar contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer that first? Can you tell the Judges?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: This document is of the -- dated the 17th of June, 1995. Two days before, on the 15th of June, an offensive began on positions of the army of Republika Srpska. So I was not in the brigade. I was out in the field, so I was not able to see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now can you please look at what is in the document. After the paragraph saying to whom the document should be delivered, please look at the next paragraph where it says: "Pursuant to the decision of the SRK Commander, you are to hand over immediately ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then can you please look at the last paragraph which says: "The materiel is to be sent to Semizovac immediately," and then it says: "Inform the command about this immediately." Can you see from this document if anything was done in relation to what is actually said in this document?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: The order exists, but we don't have any return information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now I would like to ask you about these reports that you talked about. Referring to the civilians which as was reported in the media were casualties. Was there any mention of children as casualties and, if yes, do you know the number?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: In war?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did the media report, the media of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or, let's say, the media of the Bosniak, the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: From what I can recall, during the war in 1992 to 1995, it was said that from 8 to 10.000 children were killed and that a few -- and a few months ago, they unveiled a monument in the town of Sarajevo to the children who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the meetings when it was discussed, you mentioned Josipovic, did you ever discuss or agree to fire at children or civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLAJKO BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are six minutes before the end of the session. The next witness is a protected witness, and it will take about 20 minutes to prepare, so we'll adjourn until tomorrow, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.55 p.m.,
